title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash
gist: Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash across its products with immediate access, claiming 2.5x speed, 5x fewer fabricated claims and benchmark scores that rival its pricier Argon model, while holding API pricing flat at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens even as Argon and Carbon prices double next month.

insights.claim: Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen, even in its high thinking mode, runs 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and reduces fabricated claims by more than 5x.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Speed and hallucination gains in the cheap tier improve the economics of high-volume AI workloads.
insights.quote: even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8

insights.claim: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen more than triples Gemini 3.8 Flash's score on Terminal-Bench, a code-generation benchmark.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Cheap models closing the coding gap pressures pricing of premium coding models.

insights.claim: In xhigh mode, Gemini 4 Hydrogen scored 54 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index versus 50 for Google's higher-end Argon model.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: A budget model outscoring the flagship on a popular index suggests rapid commoditization of frontier capability.

insights.claim: Gemini 4 Hydrogen offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high, and a new xhigh mode.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Tunable reasoning depth lets customers trade cost for quality within one model.

insights.claim: Google is keeping Gemini 4 Hydrogen API pricing unchanged from 3.8 Flash at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, while its Carbon and Argon models will double from $2/$10 to $4/$20 next month.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Google is widening the price gap between tiers, raising prices on premium models while holding the volume tier flat, a sign of pricing power at the top end.
insights.locator: Developers can plug into Hydrogen via the API

insights.claim: Unlike the staged Argon and Carbon rollouts that started with cybersecurity researchers and were limited to Google's most expensive subscription, Gemini 4 Hydrogen became available immediately and has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across Google's products.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Gated release of top models versus broad release of the cheap one points to capacity/safety rationing at the high end.
insights.locator: With Google’s recent Argon and Carbon releases

insights.claim: In the Gemini app and AI Studio, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available only to AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, while AI Plus and free users remain on the older 3.5 Flash-Lite model.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Model access is being used as an upsell lever for paid Google AI subscriptions.
insights.locator: Everyone will reportedly get access to Hydrogen in search

insights.claim: Google positions Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a key tool for agentic coding, handling simpler code generation and test runs cheaply, while reserving Argon and Carbon for long-horizon and security tasks.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Agentic coding workflows are being split across model tiers, increasing token volumes for cheap models.
insights.quote: Hydrogen’s speed makes it ideal for generating simpler code and running tests without blowing through token budgets
insights.locator: Google believes Hydrogen will be a key part

insights.claim: Google says integrating Gemini 4 Hydrogen into Google Search is the biggest update ever to its AI-powered search tools, with better handling of long multipart questions and more visual AI Overviews and AI Mode responses.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Deeper AI in Search affects publisher traffic and Google's ad-supported search economics.
insights.locator: Hydrogen is also being integrated with Google Search

insights.claim: Ars Technica is skeptical of Google's claim that Hydrogen's fan-out search will link to more sources, noting Google has made such promises before.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Publishers should not count on AI search sending more referral traffic.
insights.quote: but we’ve heard that from Google before
insights.locator: Hydrogen is also being integrated with Google Search
